title: Countable products of pro-etale modules are exact
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and $\mathcal R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on the small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] (for instance a constant sheaf $A_Y$, or the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$). Countable products exist in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, are computed sectionwise, $(\prod_nF_n)(U)=\prod_nF_n(U)$, and are exact: if $F_n\to G_n$ is a surjection of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules for every $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, then $\prod_nF_n\to\prod_nG_n$ is surjective.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.9 (countable products are exact in a replete topos), Proposition 3.2.3(1) (a locally weakly contractible topos is replete), Proposition 4.2.8 ($\Shv(X_{\mathrm{proet}})$ is locally weakly contractible); for modules over $\mathcal R$, products and surjectivity are those of the underlying abelian sheaves

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] to the discrete category on $\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, which is small in the fixed universes of the site. It gives a product sheaf $P=\prod_nF_n$ with $P(U)=\prod_nF_n(U)$, coordinatewise $\mathcal R(U)$-action and restrictions, and the product universal property. Apply the same result to $G_n$ to obtain $Q=\prod_nG_n$. The induced morphism $p:P\to Q$ has components $p_U((x_n)_n)=(p_{n,U}(x_n))_n$.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, limit construction; Tag 03CO, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves (2)

proof.text: Kernels in the module-sheaf category are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence for any family $a_n:F_n\to G_n$, the kernel of $\prod_na_n$ has sections $\{(x_n)_n:a_{n,U}(x_n)=0\text{ for every }n\}=\prod_n\ker(a_n)(U)$. These identifications respect restrictions and scalar actions. The product functor is additive: for families of morphisms $a_n,b_n$, its map on sections sends $(x_n)_n$ to $(a_{n,U}(x_n)+b_{n,U}(x_n))_n$, the sum of the two induced product maps. Products also preserve the zero object, so the product functor preserves kernels and is left exact; it remains to prove that it preserves epimorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian, sectionwise kernels preceding the lemma; Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits

proof.text: Assume that every $p_n:F_n\to G_n$ is surjective as a module-sheaf morphism. Fix any site object $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family] choose a covering $\{W_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ with $W_i$ affine and weakly contractible in the full site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Apply the exact evaluation functor of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits] with $X=Y$, $R=\mathcal R$, and $W=W_i$. Thus each $F_n(W_i)\to G_n(W_i)$ is a surjective map of $\mathcal R(W_i)$-modules. No constant-coefficient, finiteness, or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $Y$ or $\mathcal R$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0990, lemma-proetale-enough-w-contractible; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0946, lemma-w-contractible (1), module version as in Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles (4)

proof.text: For a target section $g=(g_n)_n\in Q(U)$, fix $i$. For each $n$ the fibre of $p_{n,W_i}$ over $g_n|_{W_i}$ is nonempty by step 3. Choose an element $x_{i,n}$ of each fibre (ordinary set-theoretic choice in the fixed universe). Then $x_i=(x_{i,n})_n\in P(W_i)$ by the sectionwise product formula and $p_{W_i}(x_i)=g|_{W_i}$. All coordinates lift on the same covering object $W_i$, rather than on separately chosen covers. Thus every target section locally lifts through $p$.

source.place: Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles, proof of (4), expanded coordinatewise lifting

proof.text: To verify surjectivity categorically without assuming a module-versus-set epimorphism comparison, let $a,b:Q\to H$ be module-sheaf morphisms with $a\circ p=b\circ p$. For each $g\in Q(U)$ use the local lifts $x_i$ from step 4. Naturality gives $a_U(g)|_{W_i}=a_{W_i}(p_{W_i}(x_i))=b_{W_i}(p_{W_i}(x_i))=b_U(g)|_{W_i}$. The equalizer sheaf axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes $H(U)\to\prod_iH(W_i)$ injective, so $a_U(g)=b_U(g)$. Hence $a=b$ and $p$ is an epimorphism. In the abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] this is the claimed surjectivity. Together with step 2 this proves exactness of countable products.
